paper.title: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents
paper.central_claim: StainFlow, a prompted-VLM process reward model that tracks visually verifiable task entities as decaying 'stains' along a trajectory (Global Entity Stain Tracking) and verifies candidate key nodes in entity-centered adaptive evidence windows (Local Stain Evidence Linking), gives more objective and fine-grained rewards than milestone-based or fixed-window PRMs, improving online-RL success on AndroidWorld by 3.2% relative and trajectory completion judgment accuracy on OGRBench by 1.8% relative over OS-Themis.
paper.claim_scope: Qwen3-VL-8B policy trained with GRPO on AndroidWorld templates (same templates for train and eval); OGRBench trajectory completion judgment with five verifiers; auxiliary verifiers Qwen3.5-VL-9B/27B.

preliminary_evidence_judgment: Read before seat scores (main text, appendices, and the PDF supplement prompts). Prompted auxiliary VLM (Qwen3.5-9B/27B) extracts screenshot-checkable entities, observes them per step (also sees the policy's actions and raw response as text context), updates decaying stain concentrations, recalls candidate key nodes, verifies them with entity-linked evidence windows, and mixes stain and key-node terms into step rewards added to GRPO outcome advantages. AndroidWorld: training tasks from the same templates with other seeds; single run per cell; 60.34 vs OS-Themis 58.62 (9B) and 62.28 vs 60.34 (27B) = ~2 tasks; 62.28 is not k/116; eta and lambda_r tuned on the same evaluation. OGRBench judgment 87.4-88.2 vs OS-Themis 86.4-86.6. Baselines re-implemented with binary step rewards. Applicable cards/expectations: rs C26 (partial); gui K19, C25; E02, E11, E12, E13, E14, E16, E28.

signatures.object: Per-step reward over a finished trajectory
signatures.information: An auxiliary VLM (Qwen3.5-VL-9B or -27B) sees the instruction and the full screenshot sequence after the episode; no environment state, no outcome label; the PRM runs retrospectively with access to later frames.
signatures.operation: Extract screenshot-checkable entities -> observe entity visibility/state per step -> stain s_t = b*c + (1-b)*gamma*s_{t-1} -> recall candidate key nodes (s >= 0.9 or |delta s| > 0) -> build evidence windows from the triggering entities' stain histories -> VLM verifies key nodes -> step reward r_t = 0.4*mean weighted stain + 0.6*key-node indicator.
signatures.output: Dense step rewards in [0,1] and an optional completion prediction.
signatures.conditions: Progress must be visible on screen as entity states; entities and attributes come from the instruction by the same VLM.
signatures.feedback: Stain decay and VLM confidence; key-node verification by VLM.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Thresholds tau_A=0.9, tau_B=0, N(t)=1, tail=3, lambda=0.4, eta=0.5 chosen by sweeps on the reporting benchmarks (E030-E032).
signatures.later_use: Step rewards enter GRPO advantage; the completion predictor is used at inference for trajectory judgment.
signatures.claimed_effect: AndroidWorld SR 60.34 (9B) / 62.28 (27B) vs 58.62 / 60.34 for OS-Themis; OGRBench overall Acc 88.2 vs 86.6 (Gemini-3-Flash).
signatures.failure_boundary: Progress that is not visible; VLM misperception; checklist concedes limited scale (E041); no analysis of policy exploitation of stain rewards.

signatures.information: Outcome reward R from AndroidWorld rule-based validation plus the step reward; both normalized per instruction group.
signatures.operation: A_t = (R - mu_R)/sigma_R + eta*(r_t - mu_P)/sigma_P with group statistics; PPO-style clipped loss with KL.
signatures.later_use: AndroidWorld evaluation on other seeds of the same templates

signatures.information: Same entity chain, key-node chain and the last three screenshots.
signatures.operation: VLM emits completion prediction and summary.
signatures.output: Binary completion decision on OGRBench trajectories.
signatures.claimed_effect: Overall Acc 88.2/F1 88.2 (Gemini-3-Flash) vs 86.6/86.2 (OS-Themis) and consistent but small margins across other verifiers
signatures.failure_boundary: Windows subset: OS-Themis higher with Gemini-3-Flash (E034, E035).

gap.author_gap: Milestone-based PRMs compress multi-solution GUI tasks into a subjective single chain; local PRMs use fixed windows that miss long-range or dilute evidence (E003).
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and relevant: sparse outcome rewards limit credit assignment in long GUI RL (the fixed UI-TARS-2 uses trajectory-level ORM/LLM-judge rewards, E044). The local-window part is supported by an evidence-span measurement (E039) but only against a one-step window; the global 'under-credits alternative valid routes' claim is argued by example and reward curves, not by a measured case of milestone failure. Neighbors OS-Themis, ADMIRE, GUI-Critic-R1, GUI-Shepherd are not in the fixed set; their characterization is by the authors.

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: iterative milestone construction/verification, but with substantial inference cost (author claim)
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: miss completion outside preset milestones (author claim)

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: trajectory-level generative ORM / LLM-judge rewards for non-verifiable GUI tasks

gap.residue: Whether entity-state tracking beats a plain per-step VLM judge with full-trajectory context; whether gains persist on unseen templates/apps; reward validity at step level.
gap.stakes: Credit assignment for long-horizon mobile/desktop GUI RL.
gap.method_response: Replace predefined milestones by entity visibility/state dynamics and replace fixed windows by entity-linked evidence windows.
gap.remaining_gap: Step-reward validity unmeasured; margin over OS-Themis is about two tasks; evaluation shares templates with training; cost claims unmeasured.
gap.unresolved: Superiority over best prior PRM is within single-run noise; no human step labels.
gap.aggregate_neighbor_check: Global milestone PRMs (ADMIRE, OS-Themis) and local step critics (GUI-Critic-R1) are re-implemented and compared, but their full texts are outside the fixed package; the local-window limitation is measured (evidence span), the milestone-subjectivity limitation is argued.

claims.text: Online RL with StainFlow rewards reaches higher AndroidWorld success than OS-Themis, ADMIRE and GUI-Critic-R1 (62.28 vs 60.34 with 27B; 60.34 vs 58.62 with 9B).
claims.baseline_control: PRM baselines with 0/1 step rewards, outcome-only, no training
claims.selection_vs_test: eta and lambda tuned on evaluation tasks; train on other seeds of the same templates
claims.result_denominator: about 2 tasks of 116; single run; headline value is not k/116
claims.allowed_conclusion: StainFlow ranks first in single-run results by about two tasks; the margin is not statistically separated.
claims.aggregate_note: 62.28 is not k/116; lambda_r/eta tuned on the reported evaluation.

claims.text: Process rewards from StainFlow improve RL over outcome-only reward.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A larger in-template gain over outcome-only reward; confounded by extra VLM verifier information.

claims.text: StainFlow improves trajectory completion judgment on OGRBench over OS-Themis/ZeroGUI/DigiRL (88.2 vs 86.6 with Gemini-3-Flash).
claims.baseline_control: DigiRL, ZeroGUI, OS-Themis with the same verifiers
claims.selection_vs_test: hyperparameters ablated on OGRBench; ZeroGUI truncated from the start
claims.result_denominator: subset sizes about 77 for MacOS; overall n not stated; margins 1.0-4.0 points
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small, mostly consistent gains across five verifiers; Windows is not a win with Gemini-3-Flash.

claims.text: StainFlow yields more objective and fine-grained step rewards (largest success/failure reward gap 0.42).
claims.result_denominator: reward gap compares differently defined reward scales
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reward distributions differ; validity of step values is not tested against humans.

claims.text: Entity-stain tracking solves the subjective single-chain milestone problem for multi-valid-path tasks.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Component ablations support that both modules matter; no direct evidence on alternative-route credit.

claims.text: StainFlow is computationally cheaper than OS-Themis.
claims.allowed_conclusion: At most two verifier calls per step by design; no measured savings.
claims.aggregate_note: Two calls per step is asserted; no measured cost.

assessment.evidence_level_note: AndroidWorld rule-based outcome checks; training and evaluation share templates and apps (rule 2 caps at online); OGRBench is an offline judgment benchmark.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported single runs: adding StainFlow step rewards to GRPO outcome reward for Qwen3-VL-8B raises AndroidWorld success from 54.31 (outcome only) to 60.34 (9B verifier) / 62.28 (27B), about two tasks above re-implemented OS-Themis, with seed-level train/test separation and hyper-parameters tuned on the reported set; as a completion judge it is 1-2 points above OS-Themis on OGRBench across verifiers.
not_supported: 'Objective' rewards (VLM-dependent, unvalidated against human step labels)

G.reason: Two concrete PRM limitations with named neighbours; the local-window one is measured (evidence spans 7.6-14.1 steps), the milestone one argued; neighbour full texts outside the fixed set.

M.reason: Entity-state dynamics and entity-linked windows target the credit-assignment gap and make predictions the ablations test (stain-only over-rewards failures; fixed window loses signal); assumes progress is visible and VLM recognition reliable.

X.reason: Equations, thresholds, windows, reward mixing, advantage, training settings, baseline adaptations, Algorithm 1/2 (listing-preserving render) and all five prompt blocks (PDF supplement) make the verifier interface reconstructable; tau_B=0 leaves candidate recall nearly unfiltered and invisible-progress/failure boundaries are not characterised.

E.measurement.reason: AndroidWorld rule-based success and labelled OGRBench are credible; step rewards are not validated against human labels, the reward-gap statistic compares differently scaled rewards, and 62.28 is not a k/116 count.

E.causality.reason: Outcome-only, three PRM baselines and three component ablations give real attribution, but eta and lambda_r were tuned on the reported evaluation, baselines are re-implemented with binary rewards, there is no plain per-step VLM judge with the same verifier, and margins are ~2 tasks.

E.holdout.reason: Training uses other seeds of the same AndroidWorld templates/apps; hyper-parameters chosen on the reporting data; no unseen templates/apps/backbones.

E.statistics.reason: One run per cell, no spread; checklist cites fixed seeds instead of error bars; ~2-task margins.

E.cost.reason: Equal epochs/batch/group and average steps reported; compute, wall-clock, tokens and verifier calls are not measured and the saving over OS-Themis is asserted.
